facts.statement: Colepiocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, meaning "knucklehead".
facts.quote: Colepiocephale (meaning "knucklehead") is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from Late Cretaceous (middle Campanian stage) deposits of Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: A partial skull of Colepiocephale was collected in 1923 from the Oldman Formation in Alberta by E.J. Whitaker.
facts.quote: In 1923, a partial skull was collected from the Oldman Formation of Alberta by E.J. Whitaker, as the only fossil found at a locality 3 mi below Bow Island ferry along the South Saskatchewan River and 200 - 300 ft below the top of the Oldman Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was initially described in 1943 by Barnum Brown and Erich Maren Schlaikjer as a species of Troodon validus.
facts.quote: GSC 8818 was first described by American palaeontologists Barnum Brown and Erich Maren Schlaikjer in 1943 as a specimen of the pachycephalosaur Troodon validus, which had earlier been given the name Stegoceras validus but was not believed to be a distinct genus by Brown and Schlaijker.

facts.statement: The species name lambei honors the Canadian palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe.
facts.quote: The species name was in honour of the deceased Canadian palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe.

facts.statement: In 2002, Thomas E. Williamson and Thomas D. Carr retained Stegoceras lambei as a distinct species, noting it was closely related to S. validum and S. sternbergi.
facts.quote: American paleontologists Thomas E. Williamson and Thomas D. Carr chose to retain S. lambei as separate in 2002, finding it as a close relative of S. validum and Stegoceras sternbergi and more distantly related to Stegoceras breve.

facts.statement: Robert M. Sullivan renamed the genus Colepiocephale in 2003 after finding it closer to Pachycephalosaurus than to Stegoceras.
facts.quote: These species and the general taxonomy of Stegoceras was reviewed in 2003 by American palaeontologist Robert M. Sullivan, who found that S. lambei was closer to Pachycephalosaurus than Stegoceras and chose to give it the new genus name Colepiocephale.

facts.statement: The genus name Colepiocephale combines the Latin word for "knuckle" and the Greek word for "head" to describe the curled appearance of the dome.
facts.quote: The name is a combination of the Latin word colepium, "knuckle", in reference to the curled knuckle-like appearance of the dome, and the Ancient Greek κεφαλή (cephale) meaning "head".

facts.statement: Thirteen other specimens of Colepiocephale lambei have been found in the Foremost Formation, now held in various Canadian museums.
facts.quote: Along with the holotype, 13 other specimens were referred to Colepiocephale lambei, held variously in the CMN, Royal Ontario Museum, Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology, and the University of Alberta Laboratory of Vertebrate Palaeontology, and all these specimens come from the Foremost Formation, part of the historical Oldman Formation.

facts.statement: A 2009 revision identified the first specimen of Colepiocephale from the Judith River Formation of Montana.
facts.quote: A redescription and revision of Colepiocephale was published by Canadian palaeontologists Ryan K. Schott and David C. Evans, and Williamson, Carr and Mark B. Goodwin in 2009, including identifying the first specimen of the taxon from the Judith River Formation of Montana.

facts.statement: Colepiocephale lived between approximately 78 and 80.45 million years ago, making it one of the oldest known pachycephalosaurs from North America.
facts.quote: The distinctiveness of Colepiocephale was supported, as well as its status as an older genus, with the Judith River specimen from sediments in Kennedy Coulee that are approximately 78 million years old, while the specimens of the Foremost are between 79.79 and 80.45 million years old.

facts.statement: Colepiocephale lambei lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Colepiocephale lambei ("cabeza de nudillos de Lambe") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Colepiocephale de dinosaurio marginocéfalo, paquicefalosáurido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Colepiocephale is considered the oldest known member of the family Pachycephalosauridae, dating to the middle Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Tiene la distinción de ser considerado como el más antiguo miembro de la familia Pachycephalosauridae, encontrándose a mediados del Campaniano, todos los demás miembros de esta pertenecen al Maastrichtiense o a finales del Campaniano.

facts.statement: Colepiocephale is classified as one of the oldest North American pachycephalosaurs from the early Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Being from the Foremost, Colepiocephale would be one of the oldest pachycephalosaurs from North America, from the early Campanian.

facts.statement: In 1987, Hans-Dieter Sues and Peter Galton argued that Stegoceras lambei and S. validum were synonyms rather than distinct species.
facts.quote: The separation of S. lambei from S. validum was not supported by the 1987 study of American palaeontologists Hans-Dieter Sues and British palaeontologist Peter Galton, who considered the two species as synonyms.

facts.statement: It is debated whether other age-equivalent specimens from the Judith River Formation belong to Colepiocephale, as their identification remains uncertain.
facts.quote: This gives the possibility that other age-equivalent specimens from Judith River could be part of the genus, though their identification is uncertain.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Colepiocephale was the only pachycephalosaur present in its specific time and geographic interval.
facts.quote: 31 specimens from the Foremost are identifiable as pachycephalosaurs, and all of them, where complete enough, show the features diagnostic to Colepiocephale suggesting it was the only pachycephalosaur within its time and space interval.

rejected.statement: Colepiocephale lambei is characterized by a domed skull lacking a lateral and posteriosquamosal shelf, a steeply down-turned parietal, and two small nodes under the posterior margin of the parietosquamosal border.
rejected.quote: C. lambei is a domed pachycephalosaur characterized principally by the lack of a lateral and posteriosquamosal shelf, a steeply down-turned parietal, and the presence of two incipient nodes tucked under the posterior margin of the parietosquamosal border.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a lateral and posteriosquamosal shelf a steeply down-turned'

rejected.statement: Charles Mortram Sternberg disputed the 1943 identification in 1945, arguing that Troodon was a carnivorous theropod and reviving the name Stegoceras while naming the new family Pachycephalosauridae.
rejected.quote: This identification was disputed by American palaeontologist Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1945, who showed that Troodon, for a time believed to be a pachycephalosaur, was instead a carnivorous theropod, who as a result revived Stegoceras as well as named the new family Pachycephalosauridae to house pachycephalosaurs.

rejected.statement: In 1945, Sternberg named the species Stegoceras lambei, using the partial skull as the holotype.
rejected.quote: Sternberg also recognized that GSC 8818 was a separate species from S. validus, and created the new species Stegoceras lambei with GSC 8818 as the holotype.
